item: A runtime ratchet drives every GET operation with the kill switch engaged and accounts for each socket, thread, file and write statement (audit 0.5.0 item 35 follow-on, P3)
refs: coordinator 27 Oct 00:21: R278, P3 runtime ratchet, floor 467, kill switch engaged, under about 2 min; audit-0.5.0/get-side-effects-2026-10-27.md
summary: tests/test_get_routes_side_effects.py drives all 467 GET operations of the app's OpenAPI schema once (about 40 s) with the network kill switch engaged, while monitors record socket connects and DNS lookups (blocked), threads started (the rate limiter's own expiry timer and the server's worker threads are not counted), files changed under the data directories, and SQL write statements through the engine. Asserts: no GET reaches a non-loopback address with the switch engaged (per-call refusal; the socket guard is not installed in a test); only the llm/* and diagnostics model routes open a loopback socket; every thread and file is in an ambient table or in a per-route table whose entries carry the reason or the finding (F1 heavy diagnostics GETs, F2 signing keys minted by custody/annotations export, both routed to RC2 by R278); no GET issues INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL. Monitor liveness is pinned (with the switch cleared /api/hazards is seen looking up usgs and gdacs; a thread, a file and a CREATE/INSERT on a TEMP table are seen). RED-WITHOUT shown: a mutant GET that starts a thread, writes a file and connects to 93.184.216.34 fails two tests naming the route. Limits stated in the docstring: empty corpus, 65 routes answer 4xx before their handler body, file changes are attributed by the request window so a background writer lands in the ambient table, the main database file is excluded because a checkpoint touches it with no write statement.
